articles.title: Differentiating Legitimate Transshipment from Origin Manipulation
articles.theme: Transshipment, rules of origin, lifecycle continuity
articles.highlight: Transshipment is not itself the problem. This article explains why global trade needs continuity of evidence to distinguish legitimate movement, genuine value addition, and origin-conferring transformation from deliberate origin manipulation, while reducing unnecessary friction for lawful supply chains.

articles.title: The Missing Assumption Behind Supply Chain Modernisation Investments
articles.highlight: Traceability is often discussed as compliance, visibility, or data capture. This article argues that the missing assumption is lifecycle continuity: the ability to preserve enough connected evidence across products, assets, organisations, and time for organisations to understand, prove, and act with confidence.

articles.title: From Lifecycle Evidence to Financial Confidence
articles.theme: Working capital, lifecycle evidence, financial decision confidence
articles.highlight: Financial decisions are increasingly made against commercial lifecycles that no institution can fully see. This article explores why lifecycle continuity should become a financial decision discipline for B2B money movement, working capital, credit, and insurance.

articles.title: Scope 3 May Be the Most Misunderstood Dataset in the Enterprise
articles.highlight: The information required to understand emissions is also information about how products move, how suppliers perform, how logistics networks behave, where costs accumulate, and where operational risks emerge across the value chain.This article explores why Scope 3 may be one of the richest sources of operational intelligence in the enterprise.

articles.title: The Balance Sheet Is Absorbing the Cost of Fragmented Coordination
articles.highlight: The balance sheet is increasingly compensating for operational uncertainty that fragmented coordination can no longer reliably manage. This article explores how instability propagates through inventory, working capital, buffers, expediting costs, and slower decisions when organisations lack continuous lifecycle visibility.

articles.title: The Hidden Coordination Crisis Beneath Net-Zero
articles.highlight: Net-zero is no longer simply an emissions problem. This article explores why the transition now depends on coordination and continuity infrastructure that can outlast executives, boards, governments, and reporting cycles.

articles.title: Net-Zero Cannot Simply Become a Future Generation’s Problem
articles.highlight: Net-zero ambitions increasingly depend on understanding what actually happens across fragmented global value chains. This article explores why sustainability disclosure struggles without lifecycle continuity, and why event-level traceability is emerging as critical infrastructure for operationally grounded emissions intelligence.

articles.title: Reconstructing Lifecycle Truth in Critical Mineral Supply Chains
articles.highlight: Critical mineral supply chains increasingly depend on proving provenance, ESG performance, and chain-of-custody continuity across fragmented global ecosystems. This article explores why current coordination models struggle to preserve lifecycle continuity, and how event-level traceability creates a continuous, verifiable operational picture across extraction, processing, transport, and manufacturing.

articles.title: What the Day Looks Like When Lifecycle Truth Exists
articles.highlight: What changes when organisations can continuously reconstruct operational reality across the lifecycle? This article explores how lifecycle truth transforms decision-making, operational coordination, resilience, and AI-enabled enterprise performance.

articles.title: Why Supply Chains Struggle to Prove What Happened
articles.highlight: Most supply chains can document transactions but still struggle to reconstruct what actually happened across products, assets, organisations, and time. This article begins with what the day looks like without event-level lifecycle continuity and why current traceability models plateau.

articles.title: Protecting Supply Chain Investment
articles.highlight: Supply chain investment increasingly depends on trusted operational visibility across ecosystems. This article examines how lifecycle traceability strengthens resilience, protects capital allocation, improves accountability, and reduces exposure created by fragmented operational data.

articles.title: Why Control Towers Have Underdelivered
articles.highlight: Most control towers aggregate signals but fail to reconstruct lifecycle continuity. This article explains why visibility alone does not create operational truth, and why fragmented timelines continue to limit resilience, coordination, and decision confidence.

articles.title: The Fracture of Time in Globalisation
articles.highlight: Globalisation connected supply chains physically but fractured them operationally across organisations, systems, and time. This article explores why fragmented visibility has become a structural coordination problem, and why lifecycle intelligence is emerging as the missing operational layer.
